processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steel blocks were cast via vacuum arc furnace.
Step-by-step hot rolling to ~11 mm followed by slow cooling in the oven.

processing_steps.method: water jet cutting (OMAX 2626, Kent, Washington, USA)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Samples precisely fabricated using a water jet cutting machine.
Austenitizing hold selected to dissolve nanoscale MC/TiC precipitates and partially suppress bainitic sheaf impingement from small prior austenite grains.

processing_steps.method: cooling from austenitization temperature to austempering temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fast enough to suppress intermediate phase transformations.
Isothermal bainitic hold at TB chosen just above the measured Ms (310 °C) to promote bainitic transformation while suppressing martensite.

processing_steps.method: final cooling to room temperature after austempering
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Final cooling step of the heat-treatment cycle in Fig. 1(a).

aliases: S4 austenitized at 1250 °C then austempered at 350 °C

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: DIL 805A dilatometer (TA Instruments, New Castle, DE, USA)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Ms = 310 °C for S4 after 1250 °C austenitization; complete bainitic transformation at 350 °C reached at 2600 s (Bt).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cylindrical specimens (5 x 10 mm^3); heating 10 K s^-1, cooling 100 K s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: Determination of austenitizing temperature (TA), Ms and bainitic transformation finish time (Bt) for S4

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Malvern Panalytical Empyrean diffractometer, Cu X-ray tube, 40 kV/40 mA, PIXcel 1D detector
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Cu Kα radiation, 40 kV; peaks (111)γ,(200)γ,(220)γ,(311)γ and (110)α,(200)α,(211)α,(220)α per ASTM E975-13
characterization_methods.purpose: Determination of retained-austenite volume fraction (Vγ) and micro-strains (εγ, εα)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss SEM (Jena, Germany) with gold sputter coating; Oxford Instruments EDX (Abingdon, UK)
characterization_methods.key_findings: S4 at TA 1250 °C / TB 350 °C shows a coarse bainitic sheaf structure with sparse bright elongated TiMoC precipitates; EDX mapping shows Fe depletion inside the Ti–Mo carbides; no micro-defects.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Etched samples, 10 µm scale bar images
characterization_methods.purpose: Morphology and chemistry of precipitates in S4 under different heat treatments
characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX)

characterization_methods.key_findings: For S4: ferrite-free TA = 1016 °C, Tcd = 1134 °C; only S4 TTP panel is a multi-system plot showing TiMoC and (Fe,M)xCy bands; TA 1250 °C/1150 °C (900 s), TB 350 °C (Bt 2600–3000 s), TB 320 °C (Bt 3500 s).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Equilibrium step calculations; TTP for cooling rate 100 K s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: Predict ferrite-free TA, carbide-dissolution temperature (Tcd) and TTP of the S4 steel

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Cooling rate 100 K s^-1; simulated for T_A 1250 °C and 1150 °C (900 s); austempering temperatures TB 350 °C (Bt 2600–3000 s) and TB 320 °C (Bt 3500 s)
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Phases considered: fcc, bcc, liquid, κ-carbide, hcp carbide, AlN, TiCN–TiMoC; carbide systems Ti-Mo-C and (Fe,M)xCy
computational_details.simulation_method: Precipitation kinetics (time-temperature-precipitation, TTP) modelling using heterogeneous nucleation theory (dislocation and grain-boundary sites, ortho-equilibrium transformation); volumetric misfit considered
computational_details.software_used: MatCalc (Version: 6.01 (rel 1.003), Institute of Materials Science and Technology, TU Wien, Wien, Austria)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: TTP results compatible with SEM observations (Fig. 10): (Fe,M)xCy and MoC precipitation retarded/suppressed in S4 by the Ti–Mo–C system; no new secondary precipitates detected during austempering within SEM resolution.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: S4 chemistry (C 0.87, Al 5.76, Mn 0.97, Si 0.30, Mo 0.48, B 0.0026, Ni 0.78, Ti 0.10 wt.%); Temperature axis starting at 400 °C
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: bcc, fcc, κ-carbide, hcp, (Fe,M)xCy, AlN and TiC systems
computational_details.simulation_method: MatCalc equilibrium step calculations of phase fractions vs temperature
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: MatCalc-predicted ferrite-free TA (1016 °C) used with dilatometry/LOM to select the applied TA; predicted Tcd 1134 °C.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: absence of micro-defects at Ti–Mo–C carbides
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: A primary characteristic of Ti–Mo–C complex carbides is the absence of micro-defects within the microstructure (Fig. 10(a),(b),(c)); no micro-void formation.

interfaces.interface_notes: EDX mapping showed depletion of Fe within the complex carbides, confirming their TiMoC composition; Ti-rich carbides suppressed formation of deleterious (Fe,M)xCy or unmodified MoC particles.
interfaces.phase_evolution: TiMoC complex carbides (and limited free TiC) form predominantly above the austempering temperature, i.e. during cooling/prior processing; no new secondary precipitates detected during austempering within SEM resolution, consistent with TTP calculation.

precipitates.distribution: bright elongated particles, longitudinally aligned; located at phase and grain boundaries

structures.overall_structure: Coarse nano-bainitic sheaf/lamellar microstructure consisting of bainitic ferrite and retained austenite, with trace (<1.0 %) polygonal ferrite and bright elongated TiMoC precipitates; no micro-defects observed.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Product of strength and elongation (PSE) of S4 at TA 1250 °C/TB 350 °C = 11,700 MPa·%; lower than S4 at TA 1150 °C/TB 350 °C (13,380 MPa·%) and TA 1150 °C/TB 320 °C (13,600 MPa·%)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All tensile specimens heat-treated using DIL 805A dilatometer applying the thermal cycle of Fig. 1(a).
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: ASTM E8 sub-size round specimens (12.5 mm gauge length, 2.5 mm diameter, 7 mm shoulder length)

unmapped_findings: Ms for S4 = 310 °C after austenitizing at 1250 °C, which is 5 °C higher than 305 °C measured after 1150 °C austenitization (difference within experimental scatter) [b0036, b0038, figure_005, b0088].
Bainitic transformation finish time (Bt) for S4 at TA 1250 °C / TB 350 °C = 2600 s; S4 incubation time was 50–60 s across all investigated parameters [b0057].

Product of strength and elongation (PSE) for S4 at TA 1250 °C / TB 350 °C = 11,700 MPa·% (UTS ~1410 MPa, El 8.3 %); lower than PSE of S4 at TA 1150 °C/TB 350 °C (13,380 MPa·%) and TA 1150 °C/TB 320 °C (13,600 MPa·%) [b0064].

Hardness (HV30) series reported in Fig. 7 for the eleven TA/TB conditions of S1–S5 reading left to right: 464, 497, 465, 500, 443, 457, 464, 479, 467, 459, 493 HV30; overall HV30 across alloys ranged 450–500 HV30 with higher values at lower TB except steel S4. The exact column-to-condition mapping for the S4 TA1250/TB350 column is not stated outright and is therefore not assigned as a firm value [b0061, figure_007].
S4 chemical composition (wt.%): C 0.87, Al 5.76, Mn 0.97, Si 0.30, Mo 0.48, B 0.0026, Ni 0.78, Ti 0.10 (belongs to alloy_s4 as a whole but underlies this sample) [b0018, table_001].
The 'best average and maximum elongation of 10 and 12 %' for S4 was achieved at TA 1150 °C / TB 350 °C, NOT at this sample's TA 1250 °C condition, and is therefore not attributed here [b0091].

MatCalc predicted C-dissolution temperature Tcd = 1134 °C and ferrite-free TA = 1016 °C for S4; complete dissolution of MC-type (Fe,M)xCy carbides predicted near 1134 °C for S4 [b0033, b0038, figure_004].

For S4, Ti microalloying led to coarsening of MoC into more complex TiMoC precipitates predominantly formed at temperatures above austempering; the added 1250 °C schedule dissolves nanoscale MC/TiC precipitates and partially suppresses bainitic sheaf impingement caused by small prior austenite grains at 1150 °C [b0095, b0113].
